newsitem.title: HAITI: First Miss Haiti beauty pageant sells out.
newsitem.headline: First Miss Haiti beauty pageant sells out.

text.p: Haiti's first beauty pageant crowned a 24-year-old student as Miss Haiti 1996 and may help buff the tarnished image of the Western Hemisphere's poorest nation, the pageant's promoter said on Sunday.

Katia Brisson, a medical student who studies in the neighbouring Dominican Republic, was crowned late on Saturday taking the event's top prize, about $8,000. Average annual per capita income in Haiti is about $250.
The sold-out contest, held at an outdoor concert venue in La Boule, just outside Port-au-Prince, probably was not a financial boon for Haitians, though.
Promoter Rodney Daniel said the pageant turned a profit, selling out 4,000 tickets at $50 each. He estimated the cost of the event at $160,000.

But groups of Dominicans, sitting at tables just behind the judges, said they had received the contracts to put together the glitzy sets and sound and lighting systems, and paid little to the Haitians hired to do much of the work.
"We hired Haitians to do some of the lower tasks, but honestly they weren't paid very much," said one of the Dominican contractors on the condition of anonymity.
The event's financial backers, from some of the richest families in Haiti, would benefit from the pageant, he added.
Promoters said the contest's major accomplishment would be to counter the negative news that usually comes out of the Caribbean nation.
"Haiti needs to improve its image," Daniel said. "An event like this is what is needed if Haiti is ever going to rebuild its tourism sector."
Haitians who could afford tickets said they were excited about the event, which snarled city traffic as pageant-goers headed home early on Sunday morning.

"I think we just showed the world how beautiful and intelligent Haitians can be," said Evans Chery, who was sleeping on the hood of his car waiting for thousands of cars to move. "The answers the contestants gave in the communication section beat all the air-headed responses I've heard watching Miss USA pageants."
Judges said an eloquent response given by Brisson to a question about domestic violence was what put her over the top. Among the judges was the current Miss Dominican Republic.
The pageant, which attracted 21 contestants, was the first ever in Haiti. In past years, the government simply selected a Haitian woman to compete in the Miss Universe pageant.
